text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc said its Centeon LLC joint venture with Germany's Hoechst AG is voluntarily recalling all its in-date lots of albumin products as a precaution against risk of bacterial infection.
Centeon is taking this precaution because some vials of its Albuminar and Plasma Plex were cracked in transit, Rhone-Poulenc Rorer said.
Rhone-Poulenc Rorer said the recall costs combined with potential lost sales could cut the consensus estimate for its 1996 earnings by 10 or 12 percent.
Rhone-Poulenc Rorer's consensus 1996 earnings estimate was $3.56 a share, according to First Call's survey of analysts.
In 1995, the company reported earnings of $2.43 a share.
Albumin is a volume expander that is often used in critical care settings, such as surgery and in the treatment of shock, trauma and burns.
Trading in Rhone-Poulenc Rorer shares, which closed yesterday at 73-5/8, was delayed.
